chunks: And he narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Uthafir, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the time of the Maghrib prayer, so he said: 'When it is easier for you and you are able in your prayer, and you are in need of your affairs, then you have the right to delay it until a quarter of the night.' He said to me: 'This is [the ruling], and he is a witness in his town.'
ai.seo_question: What is the permissible time range for delaying the Maghrib prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia juristic principle of *rukhsa* (concession), allowing Maghrib to be delayed until a quarter of the night (roughly 90 minutes after sunset) when practical needs arise. The condition of being a 'witness' (*shahid*) in one's town implies active participation in community affairs, distinguishing this flexibility from the strict obligation of *jam'* (combining) prayers during travel or hardship. This reflects the Imams' pragmatic approach to balancing ritual purity with daily life demands.
